Connect to a VPN using the SoftEther protocol. Use TAP for Layer 2 connections with root access, or TUN for Layer 3 connections without root. Manage multiple profiles and their server certificates, and select VPN traffic using per-app and address rules.\n\nUnofficial SoftEther VPN is an independently maintained open-source client that includes parts of the SoftEther VPN source code under Apache License 2.0. TUN uses UTF-8 by default. Select GBK if the server account uses a GBK-encoded password with non-ASCII characters.
TAP uses UTF-8. The saved password encoding applies when using TUN.

TAP works at Layer 2 (data link) and requires root access. The native SoftEther client carries Ethernet frames and supports LAN broadcasts, multicast, per-app routing, and address bypass. The VPN network and Android configure IPv6.

On some systems such as HyperOS, the Wi-Fi icon may show an exclamation mark when the TAP adapter becomes the system default network, even while traffic is working. Check Android network validation in Network details on the Home screen.

TUN works at Layer 3 (network) and requires no root access. Android VPN forwards IPv4 traffic and IPv6 traffic when enabled. Per-app and address routing rules work together to choose traffic for the VPN. Address rules support IP addresses, CIDR subnets, and exact domains.
